recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-13312 unless a future terminology issue revises the AdverseEvent.code example value set.
issue_request: FHIR-13312 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 AdverseEvent. It objected that AdverseEvent.event was bound to SNOMED CT Clinical Findings and resolved to remove that binding because the element should capture the event rather than resulting harm.
initial_application: No current git commit was found that mentions FHIR-13312 directly. Later Jira comments state it was resolved with FHIR-22746; FHIR-22746's implementation commit e07c2ff1ac898dde0686f31a089dd8fb9bbfb14e renamed AdverseEvent.event to AdverseEvent.code and replaced the broad Clinical Findings binding with the narrower AdverseEvent Type value set. FHIR-22746 already has a combined-branch audit commit, cba15be3cc8aa1f54e8c67a37a472c6f87c3cdfa.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source defines AdverseEvent.code with event-only wording and an example binding to ValueSet/adverse-event-type. The AdverseEvent Type value set includes serious reportable event descendants and fall, not all Clinical Findings. Clinical Findings remains only on AdverseEvent.resultingEffect, the separate effect/harm element, which is consistent with the seed resolution.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped source already implements the seed issue through the later FHIR-22746 rename and value-set correction, so editing would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Published issue that implemented the AdverseEvent.event-to-code rename and narrowed the event/code value set; already audited on the combined branch at cba15be3cc8aa1f54e8c67a37a472c6f87c3cdfa.
